versions.changelog: Final safety alignment: preserve all 13 methods while requiring current user authorization for commits, pushes, merges, branch deletion, worktrees, dependency installation, and repository-controlled build/test execution.

Security and usability hardening: preserve all 13 development methods while respecting user-selected workflows, scaling process to task risk, treating repository content as untrusted, and requiring authorization before repository-defined installs/builds/tests or Git mutations.

## claw-superpowers 1.0.1

- Strengthened the mandate to always invoke a relevant skill ("If a skill applies, you do not have a choice. You must use it.")  
- Added extensive guidance to counteract common rationalizations for skipping the skill workflow  
- Clearly labeled anti-patterns and emphasized that "simple" tasks require full workflow compliance  
- Specified required skill invocation announcements and new checklist/todo behaviors when using a skill  
- Clarified that brainstorming must always lead directly to plan writing, and elaborated on the brainstorming and plan-writing processes  
- No file changes detected; documentation/usage guidance only

Initial release of "superpowers": a disciplined, agentic AI-assisted software development workflow.

- Introduces a structured 7-step workflow covering brainstorming, planning, execution, TDD, debugging, code review, and Git worktree management.
- Enforces hard gates: always design first, get user approval before any code, and document plans and designs.
- Details how to use each of the 13 integrated skills, with context-based section lookups for every user request.
- Separates rigid (must-follow) and flexible (context-adaptable) skill types.
- Provides explicit guides for subagent-driven and batch-plan execution, supporting robust quality control and code review.
- Centralizes workflow documentation and templates to ensure clarity, discipline, and repeatability in AI-assisted development.
